text: A person with long brown hair seen from behind fills picture-left, the low sun glows at upper picture-right above the treeline, and a soft blurred grass field fills the bottom right.
intent: This photo seems to emphasize the glowing strands of hair as the sun shines through them (personal reading).

title: Shoot into the low sun with it just beside the head
why: Low sun behind the subject shines through thin hair edges, so they become the brightest textured area in the frame.

items.where: Picture-right edge of the hair, middle to lower frame
items.effect: Bright, detailed strands pull the eye first.
Dark trees make the stray strands on the hair's left outline stand out.
The darker side facing the camera confirms the light comes from behind.
The bright glow balances the heavy dark hair mass on the left.

summary: A single low sun from behind and to picture-right rims the hair and fills the air with warm haze.
direction: From behind the subject, slightly to picture-right, near the horizon.
cues: Glowing strands on the hair's picture-right edge
Darker shoulder and back at lower picture-left
Washed-out haze and faint flare at center-right
Bright sky above the treeline at upper picture-right
planA: Low sun shortly before sunset, unblocked by clouds.
planB: Sun somewhat higher, with the warmth and haze strengthened in editing.
test: On location, check whether the sun sits close to the treeline and shadows on the ground point toward the camera.

summary: The dark hair mass anchors picture-left while open bright field and sky fill picture-right.
viewpoint: Camera roughly at shoulder height, close behind the subject, held level.
order: first look: glowing hair strands at center
second look: bright sun area at upper picture-right
third look: dark treeline at upper picture-left

observe: Find where the low sun sits and what lies behind your subject, dark trees or open sky.
decide: Decide that the sun goes behind the subject so it lights the hair edges.
adjust: Step sideways a little at a time until the sun sits just outside the head's outline.
check: Hair strands glow on the sun side and the frame shows a soft haze without the sun swallowing the head.

fixed: Same subject, pose, sun, and framing distance.
change: Step sideways so the sun hides directly behind the head.
expect: The rim glow would wrap around the whole head outline and the upper picture-right sky would get darker.
gain: Cleaner contrast and less washed-out haze across the frame.
lose: The bright sun area that balances the dark hair on picture-left.

prep: An open field or park with trees in the distance, about 30-60 minutes before sunset; starting point: expose so the brightest hair strands keep their detail.
a: Shoot from behind the person with the sun just outside the head on picture-right.
b: Same as A, but step sideways until the sun is hidden behind the head.
check: Compare which shot shows more glowing individual strands and whether the face side stays readable but dark.

items.scene: Beach at sunset with a friend
items.how: Stand behind them so the sun sits just beside their head over the water.
items.fits: works when the person has loose hair or fine edges like fabric or a hat brim.
items.not: does not work when the sun is high and the light falls on top of the head.

items.scene: Cyclist on a street at low sun
items.how: Shoot toward the sun so it lights the rider's outline and wheel spokes.
items.fits: works when the background behind the edges is in shade.
items.not: does not work when a bright wall or sky sits behind every edge.

candidates: Shoot into low sun beside the head: chosen, supported by glowing strands, dark near side, and haze.
Shallow depth of field to blur the field: not chosen, the aperture cannot be confirmed from the image.
Place the hair edge against the dark treeline: not chosen, it only helps the hair's upper-left outline.
unknowns: Whether warmth and haze were added in editing
Whether any reflector filled the near side
